approaches.name: Sort, then compare neighbours
approaches.intuition: After sorting, equal values sit next to each other, so a duplicate is any adjacent equal pair.
steps: Sort a copy of the array
Compare each element with the next
Return true at the first equal pair
approaches.time: O(n log n) for the sort
approaches.space: O(n) for the sorted copy (O(1) if you may reorder the input)

approaches.name: Hash set of seen values
approaches.intuition: Stop as soon as a value repeats; a set makes the membership test constant time.
steps: Return true if the value is already in the set
pitfalls: Comparing lengths of the list and the set also works, but it always reads the whole input.

talkTrackMd: Give both answers: sorting is fine when memory is tight, a set is the fast one. State the trade-off: O(n) time with O(n) space against O(n log n) time with little extra space.
